verdicts.trueWording: making this a 4-day trip at best
verdicts.note: Raw HTML, HTTP 200. Word-for-word in the DM-facing prose under the h2 'Trek to Ten-Towns' (12 miles per day over ~50 miles); the numeral form of the same four-day span as index 902, confirming the digits/words split by register.

verdicts.trueWording: better to simply describe the day's travel in a single sentence
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: "Wizards' own encounter" - the page bylines James Haeck, a D&D Beyond columnist described there as a freelancer for WotC, not WotC editorial; in July 2020 D&D Beyond was Fandom-owned, and the only Wizards mark on the page is a boilerplate site-footer copyright.
verdicts.note: Raw HTML, HTTP 200. The advice limb is fully supported word-for-word: where nothing special is around, one sentence beats a litany of uninspired descriptions. Only the authorship attribution overreaches; cite it as publisher-hosted, as indices 902/903/905 do.

verdicts.trueWording: the largest of the ten settlements that make up Ten-Towns

verdicts.trueWording: rare that a boxed text that includes a paragraph break
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: "twice as long as it should be" - the page names no factor, saying only that such a boxed text isn't already too long by half, an idiom that will not carry a numeric reading; it also exempts introductory passages, which the claim's 'usually' does not capture.
verdicts.note: Raw HTML, HTTP 200. Quote word-for-word in the 'Don't Overdo It' subsection, which does sit under the claim's cited 'Using Boxed Text Your Way' heading. The advisory direction (limit boxed-text length; a paragraph break signals excess) is supported; only the quantification is invented.

Note the advice is one-directional and conditional - third-person objective to second-person subjective, when players tend to lose focus - slightly narrower than the claim's 'between them'.

verdicts.trueWording: the text mentioned the runes alongside other, less important details
verdicts.note: Raw HTML, HTTP 200. Word-for-word under the 'Boxed text' heading of the post (dated 15 Nov 2012, not 2016 as the claim's date field says). Every limb holds: the setting is the 2012 GEN CON D&D Championship, the runes were load-bearing (disabling them lowered the arcana DCs), and they went unmarked - the author's team missed their significance while every team heard the same text.
